The test image shows a tomato **leaf** with distinctive circular/ring-spot patterns scattered across the upper surface — lighter green concentric rings swirling against darker green tissue, with a few small brown necrotic spots. No powdery coating, no V-shaped lesions, no obvious yellowing halos.

Key features: concentric ring-spot patterns with blurred margins, small brown necrotic areas — strongly pointing to **Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus**.

Let me confirm with one reference image.

The TSWV reference shows bronzing and scattered dark spots — the test image differs in having more pronounced circular ring-spot swirling patterns. However, the TSWV description explicitly mentions "concentric ring patterns" and "lesions with blurred margins," which matches the swirling rings in the test image. Small brown necrotic spots are also present, consistent with TSWV. CMV mentions ring-spots too, but the test image lacks the mosaic/shoestring leaf deformation typical of CMV.

The ring-spot patterns centered on necrotic points with blurred margins are the key diagnostic feature pointing to TSWV.
